newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-HINGIS CONTINUES WINNING WAYS AT EUROPEAN INDOORS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS CONTINUES WINNING WAYS AT EUROPEAN INDOORS.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis, fresh from her first tournament win, crushed Japan's Naoka Sawamatsu 6-0 6-1 in her opening match at the European indoor championship on Tuesday.

Hingis, the fifth seed, continued to display the brilliant form she showed on way to her victory in Filderstadt on Sunday, needing just 49 minutes to dispatch Sawamatsu, ranked a respectable 31 in the world.
Despite the one-sided score, the 16-year-old Swiss actually began play slowly facing break-point in the opening game.
But with the partisan Swiss crowd offering support, Hingis, ranked a career-high nine in the world, quickly regrouped overwhelming Sawamatsu with her speed and precision baseline shots.
Hingis brought the drubbing to a merciful end with a pair of aces and a winning serve in the final game.
A semifinalist at the U.S. and Italian Opens this year, Hingis can expect a tougher test in the second round when she meets world number 17 Irina Spirlea of Romania.
American Jennifer Capriati took another step in her comeback with a decisive 6-3 6-4 over Argentina's Gabriela Sabatini.
Sabatini, who has struggled with injuries this year, double faulted four times on the way to dropping the first set.
Neither player appeared willing to take control of the second set each trading breaks twice.
Capriati finally broke Sabatini a third time to take the match handing the 26-year-old Argentinian her second consecutive opening round defeat.
Capriati's compatriot Lisa Raymond joined her in the second round with an upset 6-2 7-5 win over Natasha Zvereva of Belarus.
The tournament's top four seeds, including, number one seed Conchita Martinez of Spain will see their first action in on Wednesday after receiving opening round byes.
